title: Computer science
label: computer_science
description: This format is used for computer science and software engineering papers, where systems or algorithms are developed and tested.
abstract:
Key aspects:

* Sentence 1. Introduce the broader scientific or technological challenge motivating the research. Do not describe the present study yet.
* Sentence 2. Describe the specific computational problem or limitation addressed by the work.
* Sentence 3. Present the proposed algorithm, model, framework, or computational approach.
* Sentence 4. Summarize the experimental setup, datasets, benchmarks, or evaluation methodology.
* Sentence 5. Report the main results, performance improvements, and broader implications of the proposed solution.

sections.title: Introduction (with related works)
sections.content: Introduction to the problem in the context of the state of the art, the goals of the research, and the motivation. The introduction can expand the points covered in the abstract, except for the conclusions and results that belong to the specific sections of the article.

sections.title: System Design/Methodology
sections.content: Detailed description of the algorithms, models, or systems being proposed or implemented.

sections.title: Implementation
sections.content: Explanation of the implementation of the proposed system or algorithm.

sections.title: Experiments and Results
sections.content: Presentation of benchmarks, performance data, and experimental results.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.content: Analysis of results, comparison with other approaches, and limitations.

sections.title: Acknowledgment
sections.content: Acknowledgment of any support or resources.

sections.title: Conclusions
sections.content: Summary of the contributions, results, and potential future work.

title: Applied math
label: applied_math
description: This format is common for applied mathematics, numerical analysis, and mathematical modeling papers. It focuses on theory, methods, numerical validation, and analysis of results.
abstract:
Key aspects:

* Sentence 1. Introduce the broader scientific, mathematical, or numerical challenge motivating the research. Do not describe the present study yet.
* Sentence 2. Present the specific mathematical formulation, equation, or modeling problem being investigated.
* Sentence 3. Describe the analytical, numerical, or computational methods used to solve or analyze the problem.
* Sentence 4. Summarize the validation procedure, numerical experiments, or theoretical verification.
* Sentence 5. Present the main findings, mathematical insights, and implications of the results.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: A brief overview of the research problem, objectives, and problem motivation. The introduction can expand the points covered in the abstract, except for the conclusions and results that belong to the specific sections of the article.

sections.title: Theoretical Basis
sections.content: Background on the mathematical theory, methods, or models that are used in the paper.

sections.title: Methodology
sections.content: Explanation of the approach or methods developed or applied in the research.

sections.title: Numerical Results
sections.content: Presentation of numerical experiments, data, and results obtained using the proposed methods.

sections.title: Analysis
sections.content: Interpretation of the numerical results, comparison with theory or other methods.

sections.title: Acknowledgment
sections.content: Acknowledgment of any support or funding received during the research.

sections.title: Conclusions
sections.content: Summary of the findings and potential directions for future research.

title: Physics papers
label: physics_papers
description: This format is typical for physics papers, especially in theoretical and experimental physics, focusing on explaining new findings or experimental setups.
abstract:
Key aspects:

* Sentence 1. Introduce the broader physical phenomenon, scientific challenge, or theoretical context motivating the research. Do not describe the present study yet.
* Sentence 2. Describe the specific physical phenomenon, hypothesis, or system being investigated.
* Sentence 3. Summarize the theoretical framework, simulations, or experimental setup.
* Sentence 4. Present the principal findings, observations, or measured results.
* Sentence 5. Explain the scientific implications, theoretical significance, or future directions arising from the results.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Overview of the problem and objectives, with a brief summary of relevant background. The introduction can expand the points covered in the abstract, except for the conclusions and results that belong to the specific sections of the article.

sections.title: Theory and Models
sections.content: Presentation of the theoretical framework or models used to analyze the problem.

sections.title: Methodology/Experimental Setup
sections.content: Details about the experimental methods, setup, or simulations performed.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: Presentation of experimental or theoretical results, often including graphs and tables.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.content: Interpretation of results in the context of the theory and comparison with previous work.

sections.title: Acknowledgment
sections.content: Acknowledgment of contributions, funding, or support.

sections.title: Conclusions
sections.content: Concluding remarks and potential implications or future work.

title: Social sciences
label: social_sciences
description: This format is common in social sciences (e.g., sociology, psychology, economics) with a focus on theory, research questions, and empirical validation.
abstract:
Key aspects:

* Sentence 1. Introduce the broader social, behavioral, or theoretical issue motivating the research. Do not describe the present study yet.
* Sentence 2. State the specific research question, hypothesis, or social problem being investigated.
* Sentence 3. Describe the empirical methods, participants, datasets, or analytical framework used.
* Sentence 4. Present the main findings or empirical observations.
* Sentence 5. Explain the theoretical, social, or practical implications of the results.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Introduction to the research problem, its importance, and objectives. The introduction can expand the points covered in the abstract, except for the conclusions and results that belong to the specific sections of the article.

sections.title: Literature Review
sections.content: Review of existing literature and theoretical frameworks relevant to the research.

sections.title: Research Questions/Hypotheses
sections.content: Clear presentation of the research questions or hypotheses being tested.

sections.title: Methodology
sections.content: Explanation of the research design, sampling, and data collection methods.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: Presentation of statistical analyses or qualitative findings.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.content: Interpretation of results in relation to the hypotheses and existing literature.

sections.title: Acknowledgment
sections.content: Acknowledgment of any assistance or funding.

sections.title: Conclusions
sections.content: Summary of findings and suggestions for future research or practical applications.

title: Biological sciences
label: biological_sciences
description: This structure is common in agricultural sciences, agronomic sciences, biology and health sciences, where experiments or observations are the focus and methods need to be reproducible.
abstract:
Key aspects:

* Sentence 1. Introduce the broader biological, agricultural, environmental, or health-related challenge motivating the research. Do not describe the present study yet.
* Sentence 2. State the objective of the experiment, observation, or biological investigation.
* Sentence 3. Summarize the methodology used, emphasizing reproducibility and experimental design.
* Sentence 4. Present the key findings, observations, or statistically relevant results.
* Sentence 5. Explain the main conclusion and the biological, agricultural, clinical, or ecological implications of the findings.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Introduction to the research question, background, and objectives. The introduction can expand the points covered in the abstract, except for the conclusions and results that belong to the specific sections of the article.

sections.title: Background
sections.content: Review of relevant biological concepts, previous research, or disease models.

sections.title: Materials and Methods
sections.content: Detailed description of the materials, techniques, and experimental methods used.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: Presentation of experimental data, often with figures and tables.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.content: Interpretation of the results, comparison with previous research, and possible clinical implications.

sections.title: Acknowledgment
sections.content: Acknowledgment of any financial or academic support.

sections.title: Conclusions
sections.content: Summary of results, implications for practice, and future research directions.

title: Chemistry reports
label: chemistry_reports
description: In chemistry and chemical engineering, this format is used to report on experimental methods, systems design, and reactions or materials.
abstract:
Key aspects:

* Sentence 1. Introduce the broader chemical, material, or industrial challenge motivating the research. Do not describe the present study yet.
* Sentence 2. Describe the specific chemical reaction, material, process, or engineering problem being addressed.
* Sentence 3. Summarize the experimental procedures, synthesis methods, or system design used.
* Sentence 4. Present the principal experimental results, reaction outcomes, or material properties obtained.
* Sentence 5. Explain the scientific, industrial, or technological implications of the findings.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Introduction to the chemical problem, its significance, and the objectives of the study. The introduction can expand the points covered in the abstract, except for the conclusions and results that belong to the specific sections of the article.

sections.title: Literature Review
sections.content: Overview of previous research and relevant chemical theories or models.

sections.title: Experimental Section/Materials and Methods
sections.content: Detailed description of the chemical experiments, procedures, and equipment used.

sections.title: Results and Discussion
sections.content: Presentation and analysis of experimental data, with a focus on interpreting results.

sections.title: Acknowledgment
sections.content: Acknowledgment of contributions, resources, or funding.

sections.title: Conclusions
sections.content: Summary of findings, implications for chemical processes, and possible future research.

title: Philosophy humanities
label: philosophy_humanities
description: This format is typical for philosophy and humanities papers, where the focus is on logical argumentation, analysis, and critique of existing ideas.
abstract:
Key aspects:

* Sentence 1. Introduce the broader philosophical, cultural, or theoretical context motivating the discussion. Do not describe the present work yet.
* Sentence 2. Identify the specific philosophical issue, concept, text, or debate being analyzed.
* Sentence 3. Summarize the main arguments, interpretative framework, or theoretical perspectives explored.
* Sentence 4. Present the critical analysis, comparisons, or conceptual evaluation developed in the work.
* Sentence 5. Explain the conclusions, insights gained, and implications for further philosophical or humanistic discussion.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Introduction to the central research question, context, and goals of the paper. The introduction can expand the points covered in the abstract, except for the conclusions and results that belong to the specific sections of the article.

sections.title: Literature Review
sections.content: Review of existing philosophical literature and key concepts.

sections.title: Thesis or Research Question
sections.content: Presentation of the central thesis or research question the paper seeks to address.

sections.title: Argumentation
sections.content: Logical development of arguments, philosophical analysis, or critique.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.content: Reflection on the implications of the arguments and potential counterarguments.

sections.title: Acknowledgment
sections.content: Acknowledgment of any support or contributions.

sections.title: Conclusions
sections.content: Concluding summary of the arguments and future directions for research.

title: Economics political
label: economics_political
description: In economics and political science, this format is used to present theoretical models or empirical data related to policy or economic issues.
abstract:
Key aspects:

* Sentence 1. Introduce the broader economic, political, or societal challenge motivating the research. Do not describe the present study yet.
* Sentence 2. Describe the specific economic, institutional, or policy problem being analyzed.
* Sentence 3. Summarize the theoretical framework, empirical strategy, or datasets used.
* Sentence 4. Present the principal findings, trends, or statistical results.
* Sentence 5. Explain the policy implications, recommendations, or broader significance of the findings.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Overview of the research problem, its importance, and objectives. The introduction can expand the points covered in the abstract, except for the conclusions and results that belong to the specific sections of the article.

sections.title: Literature Review

sections.title: Research Design/Methodology
sections.content: Explanation of the research methods, data collection, and analysis techniques.

sections.title: Results

sections.title: Discussion

sections.title: Acknowledgment
